_comment: The semantic rules Codex applies to a hook's stdout AFTER its JSON Schema has accepted it.
These are not in codex-hook-schemas/. The schemas are generated from the wire types and
are a strict SUPERSET of what the runtime accepts: `suppressOutput` is a declared property
of every single output schema, and is rejected at parse time on three events. One schema
comment says so outright -- 'we enforce that semantic rule during output parsing rather
than in the JSON schema'. A gate that validates only against the schemas therefore passes
on output the host will reject, which is exactly how `PostToolUse hook returned unsupported
`message` is the literal string Codex shows, so a failing assertion quotes what the user
would have seen rather than a paraphrase of it.
One honest limit: `forbidden` is asserted on the PRESENCE of the key, not on its value. The
host may well accept `suppressOutput: false`; we did not test that, because the fix removes
the key outright and the distinction cannot change the implementation.

_provenance.recipe: strings -n 2 <binary> | perl -nle 'while (/((?:PreToolUse|PostToolUse|PermissionRequest|SessionStart|SessionEnd|UserPromptSubmit|SubagentStart|SubagentStop|Stop|PreCompact|PostCompact) hook (?:returned|denied) .*?)(?=(?:PreToolUse|PostToolUse|PermissionRequest|SessionStart|SessionEnd|UserPromptSubmit|SubagentStart|SubagentStop|Stop|PreCompact|PostCompact) hook |$)/g) { print $1 }' | sort -u
_provenance.note: `-n 2` and not `-n 8`: see docs/harness-probe.md, Appendix. The event name in the decision:block rule is interpolated at runtime, which is why it is filed under `*`.
_provenance.recipe_note: The previous recipe ended the match at [a-zA-Z:.,= ], which silently TRUNCATED every message containing a hyphen -- including `PreToolUse hook returned permissionDecision:deny without a non-empty permissionDecisionReason`, which lost everything from `non-` onwards. Widening the class is not the fix: these strings are packed contiguously in the binary with no separator, so a permissive class swallows the whole blob into one match. The terminator has to be the start of the NEXT message, which is what the lookahead does. Three extracted lines still carry trailing bytes from the string that follows them; the `message` fields below are those lines cleaned, so a check asserts each message is a PREFIX of some extracted line.

*.message: <Event> hook returned decision:block without a non-empty reason

PreToolUse.message: PreToolUse hook returned reason without decision
PreToolUse hook returned permissionDecisionReason without permissionDecision
PreToolUse hook returned updatedInput without permissionDecision:allow
PreToolUse hook returned permissionDecision:deny without a non-empty permissionDecisionReason

PostToolUse.message: PostToolUse hook returned reason without decision
